findings.title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive and trivially bypassed
findings.body: `BlockedEmail.where(email: email)` does an exact, case-sensitive match on PostgreSQL, and neither the stored value nor the incoming value is normalized (e.g. with `Email.downcase`/strip). If `bad@spammers.org` is blocked, signing up as `Bad@Spammers.org` passes the block check. Both sides should be normalized to lowercase before comparing or storing. The uniqueness validation and the unique index on `blocked_emails.email` have the same case gap, so duplicates differing only by case can be inserted.

findings.title: match_count update is a non-atomic read-modify-write
findings.body: `should_block?` loads the record, does `match_count += 1` in Ruby, and saves. Concurrent signup attempts with the same email read the same value and overwrite each other, so increments are lost. Use an atomic SQL update instead, e.g. `BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all(['match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ?', Time.zone.now])`.

findings.title: Validation side effect counts each signup attempt twice
findings.body: `EmailValidator` calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?`, which writes to the database (match_count, last_match_at) on every validation. `UsersController#create` runs `user.valid?` and then `user.save`, which validates again. Every signup attempt with a matching email therefore increments match_count by 2, making the statistics wrong. More generally, any extra `valid?` call anywhere inflates the counts. Recording the match should be moved out of the validator, or done only once per attempt.

findings.title: Match statistics recorded inside the user save transaction are rolled back on failure
findings.body: Because `should_block?` saves the BlockedEmail record during the User's validation, the write happens inside the User save transaction. In `save!`/`create_for_email`, a blocked email raises RecordInvalid and the transaction rolls back, losing the match_count/last_match_at update. Statistics are then inconsistent depending on the call path (`save` vs `save!`).

findings.title: rejectedEmails array is defined on the prototype and shared/persistent
findings.body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` in `extend()` creates one array shared by every instance of the controller, and it is never cleared. If an email is rejected for a transient reason (for example 'has already been taken' because of a race), it stays rejected client-side for the rest of the page session. The array should be initialized per instance in `init` and reset when the modal is reopened.
